findings.detail: `role="status" aria-live` is on the outer `<div>` that contains the whole `<ul>` of review items, not just the summary. Two concrete consequences for the keyboard/screen-reader path through a workflow whose entire point is clicking through N flags: (1) every `Use {p}` / `Delete` / `OK` click removes the `<li>` that holds the focused button, so focus falls to `<body>` and the user must Tab back down through the config form and results bar for each one of N items; (2) because the list itself is inside the live region, each removal re-announces the full remaining list (up to `max-h-80` of rows) rather than the one thing that changed. The individual buttons are correctly `aria-label`ed and the panel does announce — this is about where the boundary sits, not a missing announcement.
findings.summary: Review panel wraps its action list in one live region; focus is lost per fix

findings.detail: `crossChecked` is derived only from `uncheckedFiles.length === 0`, which cannot distinguish "every image was cross-checked and agreed" from "no image was ever cross-checked". At line 666 `media` is `[]` whenever `doubleCheck` is false, so `reads` is `{}`, `setUncheckedFiles([])` runs, `crossChecked` becomes `true`, and `review` contains static checks only. The auto-send effect's guard (`!crossChecked` return) then passes, and a statically-clean run posts the workbook to the Zoho task with no price verification at all — the precise outcome ADR-0008 § "Auto start and auto send" says must wait for a person ("only when ... every image or PDF was cross-checked"). The trigger is narrow today: a bridge page load resets `doubleCheck` to `true` and auto-start runs before the user can reach the checkbox, so it needs the operator to untick the box and re-run manually inside the same bridge session. What would raise this to high is any change that persists the checkbox across loads (localStorage, a URL param, or a per-user default) — the gap would then be the default path, not an edge.
findings.summary: crossChecked is true when the double-check never ran, so auto-send fires unverified

findings.detail: `reads[f.file.name] = items` and the `uncheckedFiles` filter at line 681 both key on the basename, and `crossCheck` matches rows on the `Source File` column, which is the same basename. `safeFileName` in the bridge strips path parts, so a Zoho task carrying `scan-a/menu.pdf` and `scan-b/menu.pdf` — or a user picking same-named files from two folders — produces two inputs that collapse to `menu.pdf`. `reads['menu.pdf']` then holds only the last file's entries, `uncheckedFiles` reports the name as checked, and the first file's rows are cross-checked against the wrong page, yielding spurious `unconfirmed` / `price-mismatch` flags. It fails in the safe direction (extra flags hold the auto-send, never release it), which is why this is low, but it presents as the double-check being wrong rather than as a name collision.
findings.summary: Second readings keyed by bare file name collide on duplicate basenames

findings.detail: For each row of a source file the loop runs `entryNames.forEach` over every entry of that file's second reading, and each pair does `parts.some(matchPrepared)` with a substring test plus a token-set intersection. Because the second reading is designed to return roughly one entry per row, that is quadratic in the item count of a single image. It is also not a one-off: `review` is a `useMemo` on `masterData`, so the whole `reviewRows` pass re-runs synchronously on every `Use {p}` / `Delete` / `OK` / `Add` click. A 300-item menu is ~90k `matchPrepared` calls per click — noticeable but not a freeze, which is why this is low rather than high; the bound is what one model call returns for one image, so the hundreds-of-thousands-of-rows shape the performance handbook worries about is not reachable here.
findings.summary: crossCheck is O(rows x entries) per file and re-runs on every fix click

findings.detail: `addFiles` opens with a bare `{ ... }` block wrapping its entire body — an artifact of lifting the code out of the `if (e.target.files)` guard in `handleFileUpload`. It has no effect (no shadowed `let`/`const` relies on it) and adds a level of indentation to a 40-line function, which makes the nesting look deeper than it is when read against the code-smells thresholds.
findings.summary: Leftover bare block in addFiles from the handleFileUpload extraction
